channel.title: Kramer Elementary School News
channel.description: News and announcements from Kramer Elementary School, including events, activities, and important dates.

item.title: Read At Home Program and Kroger Rewards
item.description:
Read At Home (RAH) is a voluntary program for K-2nd grade students at Kramer Elementary that encourages reading at home. Students record books they've read each week on a record sheet and turn it in for rewards, which alternate between a student-selected book and a small prize.

Kroger Community Rewards: Connect your Kroger Rewards card to Kramer PTG (one nonprofit per account) and Kroger will donate a percentage of your purchases to the PTG. Sign up once at https://www.kroger.com/i/community/community-rewards

item.title: Kramer Free Pantry Available to Students
item.description:
The Kramer Free Pantry is located at the entrance of Kramer and provides free food and hygiene items to all students. Available items include cereal, fruit, vegetables, peanut butter, spaghetti, mac and cheese, soup, shampoo, and toothbrushes. For questions, donations, or suggestions, contact Chelsea Pike, Kramer Social Worker at 513-273-3511 or pikec@talawanda.org.

item.title: Reading Corner Newsletter on Decoding Skills
item.description:
The February Reading Corner Newsletter explains decoding—the foundational reading skill of recognizing letter sounds and blending them to read words. The newsletter provides grade-specific decoding activities for Kindergarten through 3rd grade via Reading Rockets website links, including a video showing how 3rd graders use syllables to decode longer words. Parents can contact Mrs. Geshan (geshanc@talawanda.org), Mrs. Kobermann (kobermanc@talawanda.org), or Mrs. Walters (waltersh@talawanda.org) with questions.

item.title: K-Mart Store Open Every Monday and Friday
item.description:
The K-Mart student store is open every Monday and Friday from when you walk in until the bell rings. It is located on the balcony between 4th and 5th grade classrooms at Kramer Elementary. item.title: Office Notes: Fees, Lunch Accounts, and Dismissal
item.description:
Student fees are now available to pay online through PaySchools or in the office with cash/check. Lunch accounts can be funded through PaySchools; accounts reaching -$50 will roll into school fees. Families can apply for free/reduced lunch by contacting the Marshall office or social worker Chrissy Rolfes at rolfesc@talawanda.org—qualifying families receive fee waivers or 85% reduction (except 5th grade Chromebook fee). At dismissal, please pull forward to the upper lot to buckle children after they enter your car to keep the process safe and efficient. Update any contact or address changes through Final Forms (address changes require new proof of residency submitted to the office).

item.description:

Register at cefcincy.org/marshall or contact Rosie Frisch at 513-907-9496.

item.title: Marshall Free Pantry Available to Students
item.description:
The Marshall Free Pantry is located at the front left side of the school near the gym doors and is open to all students. The pantry offers free food, hygiene products, and school supplies including veggies, fruit, pasta, soup, applesauce, snacks, school supplies, body wash, shampoo, and toothpaste. For questions, donations, or suggestions, contact Chrissy, Marshall Social Worker at 513-273-3611 or rolfesc@talawanda.org.

item.title: BoosterThon Glow Party Fundraiser Progress
item.description:
The BoosterThon fundraiser launched February 2nd and will culminate with a Glow Dance Party on Thursday, February 12th. The campaign has reached 57% student sign-up and 31% students with donations, raising funds toward a $15,000 goal to support students and staff. Participants from 10 states and 2 countries are involved, with top classes being Paluch (1st), Lykins (4th), and Slattery (5th). A weekend challenge offers a bonus keychain for earning $60 in donations. Register at mybooster.com.

item.title: February Reading Corner: Understanding Decoding Skills
item.description:
The February newsletter explains decoding - the foundational reading skill of recognizing letter sounds and blending them to read words (like /c/ - /a/ - /t/ becomes "cat"). Reading Rockets provides age-specific decoding activities for students: - Kindergarten activities - First Grade activities - Second Grade activities - Third Grade: A video demonstrates how students use syllables to decode longer words more easily.

item.title: February 2026 Breakfast and Lunch Menus
item.description:
Marshall Elementary's February 2026 breakfast and lunch menus are now available.

Breakfast highlights include breakfast burritos, biscuits & sausage gravy, French toast bites, breakfast pizza, pancakes on a stick, donuts, and chicken biscuit sandwiches. 100% fruit juice, apples, oranges or other fresh fruit selection and milk included with every breakfast.

Lunch highlights include nachos with taco meat, rotini & Italian meat sauce, popcorn chicken dinner roll, various pizzas, mac & cheese, chicken tenders, hot dogs, quesadillas, corn dogs, grilled cheese, and salisbury steak. Choice of milk included with every lunch.

Both menus note that items are subject to change based on product availability. No school on February 16 (Presidents Day).

item.title: Preschool Lottery Application for 2026/2027
item.description:
Talawanda Preschool is accepting lottery applications for typically developing children for the 2026/2027 school year. Applications must be completed by January 31, 2026, and the lottery will be held on February 13, 2026. Families will be notified of placement or waitlist status after February 13th. Contact Preschool Coordinator Beth Fuechsl at fuechsle@talawanda.org with questions or visit the Preschool Application.

item.title: Principal's Weekly Update from Marshall
item.description:
Principal Mrs. Jones celebrates a successful week at Marshall, highlighting students' strong academic engagement and positive behavior. Students demonstrated respect, responsibility, and readiness to learn through classroom collaboration, peer helping, and supportive friendships. The principal thanks families for reinforcing these values at home and looks forward to another great week.
